I am 68 years old, and I have worked this land for 48 years. I never went to school, but I can read the soil with my hands and the sky with my eyes. My family has six mouths — some of my children work in the factories in the city and send money home, but they always come back for the busy seasons. I have 10.1 mu and a well for irrigation, so I am not completely at the mercy of the rain.

This year, like most years, I will keep 8 mu in my wheat-maize rotation. The wheat went into the ground after National Day last autumn, and now that spring is here it needs its first topdressing and irrigation at green-up. I will irrigate three times in total — once now to wake it up, once at jointing when the stems shoot up, and once at grain filling. I use improved wheat seeds that I select from my own best ears, and I always rotary till before sowing so the soil is fine and even. For fertilizer, I know that more is not always better — too much nitrogen and the wheat falls over in a storm. I will put down about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu, mostly from urea and compound fertilizer, with some phosphorus and potassium to feed the roots. I expect around 460 kg per mu if the weather treats us kindly.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant hybrid maize the same day without ploughing — there is no time to waste between the two crops. Maize is simpler: one good irrigation when the tassels appear, a bit of fertilizer at planting and another at jointing, and two sprayings — one for weeds and one for insects. I expect about 500 kg per mu.

I keep 2.1 mu of cotton because the price for seed cotton has been decent, and I have grown cotton since I was a young bride. But at my age I cannot manage too much — the pruning, the spraying, and the picking are hard on my knees and back. I will rotary plough in April and sow improved cotton seeds. Cotton needs water at flowering and again when the bolls are forming, so two irrigations. The bollworm is a devil, so I will spray five times, mixing the medicines myself the way I have always done. I give the cotton a bit more potassium to make the bolls strong. If my daughters-in-law can come home for the picking in autumn, we should get about 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I keep only 2.1 mu of cotton because the picking and pruning are too hard on my body now.
